newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court postpones Purneft hearing to April 3.
newsitem.headline: Russian court postpones Purneft hearing to April 3.

text.p: The Moscow Arbitration Court has postponed a hearing on an appeal about the ownership of oil producer Purneftegaz to April 3, officials at oil groups SIDANKO and Rosneft said on Thursday.
The hearing was due to be held on March 19, having already been postponed from March 3.

SIDANKO, one of the top seven Russian oil groups, and state oil holding company Rosneft, have been fighting over the ownership of Purneftegaz, now officially called AO Rosneft-Purneftegaz, for several years.
Russian courts have repeatedly awarded it to Rosneft, which is due to be privatised this year.
The current case is the third fought by SIDANKO, which is suing the State Property Committee -- Russia's privatisation ministry -- and Rosneft.
OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) is one of a dozen or so vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years.
Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
SIDANKO is mostly owned by Interros-Oil, which is associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) and Bank MFK.
